name: Resumption/Retention of Sri Lankan Citizenship (Dual Citizenship)

requirements.blocker_text: Applicant is 55 years of age or older.
Holds a minimum one-year diploma or higher qualification.
Owns immovable property in Sri Lanka worth LKR 2,500,000 or more.
Holds a local fixed deposit of LKR 2,500,000 or more, held for 3 years.
requirements.fix_path: Place a 3-year fixed deposit of at least LKR 2,500,000 in a Sri Lankan bank.

requirements.blocker_text: Holds US$25,000 or more in an approved foreign-currency account for 3 years.
requirements.fix_path: Place US$25,000+ in an approved foreign-currency account for 3 years.

requirements.blocker_text: Holds US$25,000 or more in Sri Lankan Treasury Bonds or a Security Investment Account.
Is the spouse, or an unmarried child under 22, of a person who separately qualifies under one of this route's other categories.

evidence_required.document: Certificate of good conduct from local police (issued within 3 months)
Foreign passport/naturalization certificate (resumption) or permanent resident card (retention)

sources.title: Permanent Mission of Sri Lanka to the United Nations (official mission page) -- Resumption/Retention of Sri Lankan Citizenship (Dual Citizenship): for persons who lost citizenship under Sections 19-21 of the Citizenship Act 1948 by acquiring another nationality (resumption) or who face imminent loss and wish to retain Sri Lankan citizenship alongside a new one (retention); eligible via any of 7 categories -- age 55+, 1-year+ diploma/qualification, LKR 2,500,000+ immovable property, LKR 2,500,000+ 3-year local fixed deposit, US$25,000+ 3-year approved foreign-currency deposit, US$25,000+ Treasury Bonds/Security Investment Account, or as the spouse/unmarried under-22 child of a qualifying applicant; fees: US$30 processing, US$2,000 main applicant, LKR 57,500 spouse, US$500 unmarried children

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Sri Lanka). Published on tier-1 sourcing (an official Sri Lankan diplomatic mission page). MARQUEE ROUTE, GENUINELY DISTINCTIVE IN THIS DATASET: Sri Lanka's baseline rule is that citizenship is LOST automatically on voluntarily acquiring a foreign nationality (Sections 19-21) -- there is no general dual-citizenship right the way Kenya or Ghana affirmatively grant. Instead, a SEPARATE, FEE-GATED, ASSET-OR-CREDENTIAL-GATED application process exists to resume or retain Sri Lankan citizenship specifically -- a structure closer to a 'buy-back' or 'qualify-back' mechanism than an ordinary legal right. The seven eligibility categories mix genuinely different logics (an age threshold, an educational credential, three different asset/deposit tracks, and a family-derivative category) -- modeled here as seven separate requirement_groups under OR logic since satisfying any single one suffices. requirement_groups values use LKR (Sri Lankan Rupees) for the local asset tracks and USD for the foreign-currency/investment tracks exactly as the source states them -- not converted, to avoid introducing an unsourced exchange-rate assumption. This is the primary legal mechanism behind Sri Lanka's very large global diaspora (Sinhalese, Tamil, and Burgher communities spread substantially across the UK, Australia, Canada, and the Gulf, driven in large part by the 1983-2009 civil war and subsequent economic crises) reconnecting with Sri Lankan citizenship.
